description: We are a multidisciplinary student team focused on turning ideas into working solutions. Our members bring different strengths, and we share a commitment to open communication, honest feedback, and building over talking. We’re drawn to the NASA challenge because it sits where curiosity meets real-world impact. Space, Earth observation, data, hardware, and creative problem-solving all excite us. We enjoy problems without obvious answers and the early stage where ideas are pulled apart and rebuilt
summary: Sky-Fi Space Explorers is a fun, free learning platform that helps children discover space in a way that suits their age. It combines lessons, quizzes, team missions and rewards, so children learn by exploring and making decisions instead of just reading. The aim is to build curiosity about space and science in young learners.
details:
PROBLEM

Most space content is either too simple or too advanced for a child, and it is mostly passive. Children lose interest, and few resources let them apply what they learn or learn with others.

SOLUTION

Sky-Fi Space Explorers asks the child's age first, then opens content for one of three groups: Little Explorer (5-7), Junior Astronaut (8-11) and Space Commander (12-15).

FEATURES

- Age-based lessons: stars, the Sun and rockets for the youngest; gravity, planets and the ISS for the middle group; light-years, orbits and Mars launch windows for the oldest.

- Quiz: scoring above 50% unlocks a reward film, a warp-speed flight past the planets with visual effects.

- Crew missions: the child joins a crew (practice crewmates in this version) and makes decisions that depend on what they learned earlier.

- Rewards: points and six collectible badges.

- Space news: a news section with recent stories from NASA, ESA and ISRO coverage.

HOW IT IS BUILT

A single web page using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with the reward film drawn on an HTML canvas. It needs no installation or account, and progress is stored only on the child's own device, so no personal data is collected.

CURRENT LIMITS AND NEXT STEPS

Crewmates are simulated in this version. Next steps are live multiplayer crews on a safe server, more languages, a teacher dashboard and live NASA and ESA news feeds. The news section is currently a snapshot from November 2026.

SOURCES

Space facts from standard NASA educational references. News from NASA, ESA and ISRO coverage, November 2026.

AI USE

AI assistance (Claude by Anthropic) was used.
